transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I’m here because I’m scared by how I’ve been eating. Once I start, especially if I’m alone in the kitchen, it feels like I can’t stop myself. I’m telling myself the whole time, “Janet, put it away,” but I just keep going.
Have you noticed any change in your weight recently?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t been keeping close track of my weight, so I can’t say for certain if it’s changed much.
Do you usually feel guilty or ashamed after one of these eating episodes?

Yes. I feel really guilty afterward. I’ll sit there thinking I wasted food that was meant to be for everyone, and I feel ashamed, like I’m too old to still be doing this. I usually tell myself, “That’s it, I’m not doing this again,” but then it happens again.
Do you ever make yourself vomit after eating?
No, I don’t make myself throw up after eating.
Do you ever eat a large amount of food in a short period of time without feeling like you can't stop, even when you're not hungry?

Yes. A lot of times it’s after I’ve already eaten supper. I’m not hungry, really, but I’ll still go back to the pantry or the fridge and start picking at things, and then it turns into a lot more than I meant to eat.
Do you ever exercise excessively to try to burn off the calories from one of these eating episodes?
I don’t think so. I mean, I might feel like I should be more active, but I don’t go out and exercise a bunch to make up for it.
How often do these episodes of eating a large amount of food in a short period of time happen?
Most weeks, I’d say. I looked back at my kitchen calendar and the weeks I go to the food bank, and it’s usually once or twice a week. It’s been going on like that for many months now.
During these episodes, do you feel like you're in control of how much you're eating?

No, not really. That’s the part that scares me. Once I start, especially if I’m alone in the kitchen, it feels like I’ve kind of stepped aside and I can’t make myself stop, even though I’m telling myself, “Janet, put it away.”
During these episodes, do you feel like you're eating faster than you normally would?

Yes. I notice I eat really fast during those times. Like I’ll be standing at the counter with a casserole or muffins I made, and I’m just taking bite after bite so quickly I barely even taste it. It’s like I’m in a hurry, even though I’m not going anywhere.
Have these episodes of eating been affecting your daily life or relationships in any significant way?

Yes, it has some. I still make it to my volunteer shifts and the craft fairs, so I’m not just staying home all the time. But afterward, if there’s a shared meal or people are getting together to eat, I’ve started skipping those more often. I feel embarrassed, and I don’t want anyone noticing I’m upset or asking me what’s wrong.
Do you often try to limit the amount of food you eat or avoid certain types of food between these episodes of eating a large amount of food?

I’m not really sure. I don’t think I have a clear pattern with that. Sometimes I might tell myself I should eat less or be more careful, but I haven’t really noticed avoiding specific foods in a consistent way.
Have you noticed any significant fluctuations in your weight over time?
I’m not really sure. I don’t weigh myself regularly, so I haven’t noticed any big changes one way or the other.
Have you ever had periods where you lost a lot of weight, only to gain it back?
I don’t really know. I haven’t kept close track of my weight, so I can’t say there’s been a time where I lost a lot and then gained it back.
Are you afraid of gaining weight?
I don’t think I’m afraid of gaining weight exactly. I mean, I don’t love the idea, but I wouldn’t say it’s something I’m constantly scared about.
Have you ever had times in your life where your weight changed a lot, either up or down, in a relatively short period?
Not that I can clearly remember. I haven’t really tracked my weight closely, so if it changed some, I don’t think I noticed it as a big sudden shift.
Are you afraid of gaining weight or becoming fat?
I wouldn’t say I’m afraid of becoming fat. I don’t like thinking about gaining weight, but it’s not something I’m constantly worrying about.
Have you ever experienced a time when you lost a significant amount of weight?
No, I don’t think so. I can’t remember any period where I lost a lot of weight in a noticeable way.
Have you ever had a period where you gained a lot of weight in a short time?
Not that I’m aware of. I mean, my weight may have gone up gradually at times, but I don’t remember a period where I gained a lot really quickly.
Have you ever had a period in your life where your weight fluctuated significantly, going up and down in a short amount of time?
No, I don’t think I’ve had that. My weight’s changed some over time, but I haven’t noticed it going up and down a lot in a short period.
Do you ever use laxatives or diuretics to try to counteract the effects of your eating episodes?
No, I don’t use those. I’ve never really tried to make up for eating that way.
